title: Continuous Tuning of the Charge-Phase Uncertainty in a Josephson Junction
authors: Irena Padniuk, Xianzhe Zeng, Juan Carlos Cuevas, Joachim Ankerhold, Klaus Kern, Christian R. Ast
abstract: Quantum mechanics constrains conjugate observables from being simultaneously measurable with arbitrary precision. In a Josephson junction, these are the transferred electric charge and the quantum-mechanical phase difference between the superconducting domains. Which of them fluctuates determines the supercurrent: a dissipative trickle of single Cooper pairs in one limit, a coherent dissipationless flow in the other. Bridging both regimes in one device remained elusive because the Josephson and charging energies are fixed at fabrication. Here, we use the tunable tunnel junction of a scanning tunneling microscope at millikelvin temperature to vary their ratio continuously over many orders of magnitude. In this way, we monitor the smooth transition between incoherent and coherent Cooper pair flow in a single junction, revealing the quantum-to-classical transition in a controlled way.
summary: The authors demonstrate a controlled measurement of the transition between charge-dominated (Coulomb Blockade) and phase-dominated (Josephson) transport regimes in a Josephson junction using an STM tip. By continuously tuning $E_J/E_C$, they confirm the smooth crossover, validating advanced theoretical models like qIZ against direct experimental observation.
main_problem: The study aims to monitor and understand the smooth quantum-to-classical transition of Cooper pair flow in a Josephson junction by continuously tuning the ratio of Josephson energy ($E_J$) to charging energy ($E_C$).
main_result: The experiment successfully traced the full crossover from the Dynamical Coulomb Blockade (DCB) regime to the coherent, dissipationless tunneling (DCT) regime in a single device.
method: The research combines STM-based experiments to tune junction parameters with advanced theoretical modeling using Multiple Andreev Reflections (MARs) and the quantum Ivanchenko-Zil’berman (qIZ) model.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting tunnel junction whose behavior is governed by the competition between $E_J$ and $E_C$. The analysis uses theoretical frameworks like MAR theory and the qIZ model to describe current flow across different regimes.
key_observables: Current-voltage ($I(V)$) characteristics, switching current ($I_S$) vs. conductance ($G_N$), and phase rotation per tunneling Cooper pair ($\Delta\phi/\Delta n$).
important_parameters: The ratio $E_J/E_C$, the Stewart-McCumber parameter ($ eta_C < 1$ for overdamped regime), and junction conductance ($G_N$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: Theoretical models assume an ohmic environment impedance, a sinusoidal current-phase relation (which breaks down at high $G_N$), and the applicability of specific approximations like Markovianity in certain regimes.
figures_summary: Figures show the crossover of switching current from quadratic to linear dependence on conductance ($I_S$ vs. $G_N$) and illustrate MAR fits used to extract channel configurations and track phase rotation evolution.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the experimental tunability of $E_J/E_C$, then analyzing the resulting current-phase relation using MARs, and finally comparing theoretical predictions (qIZ vs. P(E)-theory) against the observed smooth crossover between DCB and DCT regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct experimental realization of controlling quantum fluctuations in superconducting circuits, which is highly relevant for understanding dissipation mechanisms in superconducting qubits and quantum computing architectures.
